source.title: Learning from setbacks: the impact of adversarial initialization on generalization performance
source.authors: Kavya Ravichandran; Yatin Dandi; Stefani Karp; Francesca Mignacco

record.tranche_reason: Tests when random-label adversarial initialization worsens test performance relative to random initialization, and finds that the effect varies with dataset structure and representation handling. This does not directly test a listed version's specified measure or setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for retraining after fitting random labels and for freezing adversarially learned features. It does not report held-out accuracy on random labels or directly test the versions' specified claims. Cited results from Liu et al. and other prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests the coexistence component of V1 in a new setting: its one-hidden-layer ReLU networks fit random labels to zero training error and also generalize almost perfectly on natural-label Gaussians. Random-label held-out accuracy is not reported. The adversarial-initialization comparisons themselves test a different claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: solution norm alone is insufficient; representation quality explains some regimes but not others, and its role depends on data structure. The authors leave the mechanisms and their theoretical characterization open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random-label pretraining followed by true-label training, but studies one-hidden-layer fully connected networks on synthetic data and a 128-example vectorized MNIST sample rather than the listed versions' settings. It also tests freezing adversarial features and resetting readout weights.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset structure and network width affect the reported comparisons; results across different draws of data can differ from results with fixed data.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label pretraining changes subsequent natural-label test accuracy; resetting the readout and freezing features has effects that depend on dataset and width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization consequences of random-label pretraining depend on initialization, representation handling, and data structure.

record.peer_reviewed: Mathematics of Modern Machine Learning Workshop at NeurIPS 2023
record.problems: Results are largely presented as curves without exact values in the text. The MNIST experiments use only 128 fixed samples and, as the authors note, substantially less randomness than the other experiments. Error bars intersect for spirals, and outcomes can differ when the data draw is fixed versus varied.

untested.parts: Held-out accuracy with random labels; the original image architectures and datasets. Absolute natural-label accuracy for spirals and MNIST cannot be established from the supplied text.
Whether test error continues decreasing beyond the width required for interpolation. Width sweeps alone do not establish this trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and tuning dependence.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and their dependence on data size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: A separate natural-label baseline result for Gaussian Experiment 1: zero training error and near-perfect test generalization. This directly records the natural-label side of V1 without conflating it with the adversarial-initialization gap.

record.verdict_notes: The significant Gaussian initialization gap coexists with near-perfect accuracy in every condition, so it does not challenge V1. No V2 verdict is justified by the untranscribed width curves. States of cannot_determine for rows linked to none concern their applicability to the listed versions, not whether the intervention comparisons occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out performance on random labels or establish that natural-label accuracy is far above chance.
Although it sweeps hidden-layer width, it does not test whether test error keeps falling beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap comparison.

relationships.reason: R1 combines zero-error random-label fitting with near-perfect natural-label generalization; Section 3.3 also explicitly reports near-perfect performance for the natural-label baseline. This supports coexistence, without testing random-label held-out accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: Random-label training reached zero error alongside near-perfect natural-label generalization, while random-label held-out performance was untested.

relation.reason: Its own experiments demonstrate zero-error random-label fitting and near-perfect natural-label generalization with the same network family.

tranche.reason: The study provides a result on V1's coexistence component in a new setting: one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on separable Gaussians. Its initialization comparisons do not contradict that component.

source_check.notes: The significant initialization gap alone does not establish coexistence; the zero-error fitting procedure and explicit near-perfect Gaussian generalization do. Exact test accuracies and random-label held-out accuracy are not reported in the text.
